text:
incident-bot: Pager: high error-rate detected for service `api-gateway` (5xx spike). Alert: 5xx-rate > 3% over 5m, source=global-edge. Escalation: oncall-kai@redwood
kai (oncall): I'm on it. pulling up grafana now. what does the spike look like?
marta: saw a cascade earlier — a bunch of 429s from rl-controller then 5xx at the gateway 1:30m into the spike. could be quota misapply.
leo: confirming from logs: gateway logs show lots of `upstream reset` and some `502 Bad Gateway` from model-proxy pool.
anjali: copying runbook for 5xx-cascade: runbook link https://confluence.redwood/5xx-cascade (quick steps: identify offending rate-limit config, check quota stores, toggle fallback routes, scale pools)
kai (oncall): running quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep model-proxy` -> some proxies are OOMKilled recently. running `redis-cli --latency` for quota-store; latency spiking.
leo: paste: ```[2024-11-02T14:12:34Z] api-gateway ERROR upstream reset by peer connection_id=0x3ff status=502
[2024-11-02T14:12:35Z] rl-controller WARN exceeded rate for tenant=acme-corp bucket=per-minute
[2024-11-02T14:12:36Z] model-proxy ERROR kv-cache miss surge, spawn delay
``` 
kai (oncall): hypothesis: a recent quota-policy rollout (tenant-level token-buckets) accidentally lowered global burst window -> many clients hit 429 -> retry storms -> model-proxy pool overwhelmed -> gateway 5xx. check config rollouts.
marta: I can see a rollout in feature-ops: `quota-policy/v2` pushed ~14:05 UTC (2 hours ago). patch shows per-tenant defaultBucket=50 -> mistakenly 5 in prod for some tenants.
anjali: can we confirm which tenants are affected? support-ops, please run a query on recent 429 emits to map tenants.
support-ops: running query: `select tenant, count(*) from metrics.requests where status=429 and ts > now() - interval '10 minutes' group by tenant order by count desc;` -> top offenders: acme-corp (12k), beta-inc (9.4k), partner-x (3.3k)
leo: acme-corp is on Dedicated and had a burst of traffic due to a scheduled job at 14:00 UTC. That explains the initial spike.
kai (oncall): mitigation plan (fast): 1) pause quota-policy rollout 2) temporarily increase per-tenant burst for dedicated pools 3) enable model fallback route to cpu-quantized variant for acme-corp 4) scale model-proxy pool by +20% 5) communicate to customers
marta: executing step 1: `kubectl rollout pause deploy/quota-policy -n infra` -> paused. patch id 8f3b
anjali: step 2: patching rl-controller config: ```yaml
rate_limiter:
  default_burst: 500  # temp bump
  per_tenant_overrides:
    acme-corp: 2000
``` applying now
leo: scaling model-proxy: `kubectl scale deploy/model-proxy --replicas=12 -n inference` (was 10). watching pod startup.
kai (oncall): enabling fallback route for acme-corp: updated routing policy to send to `model-quantized-v1` for non-critical latency-sensitive requests. command: `redwood route update --tenant acme-corp --fallback model-quantized-v1`
support-ops: sending proactive msg to top affected customers: "We're investigating elevated error rates affecting inference calls; temporary mitigation in progress. We'll update in 15m." drafting now.
leo: after scale and rate-limiter bump, 5xx rate dropped from 3.4% -> 0.8% in 6m. 429s also dropping. dashboard: link https://grafana/graphs/5xx-spike
anjali: we should check token-bucket sync across regions — noticed some tokens weren't replicated due to backlog. running replication worker health check.
kai (oncall): good catch. firing `systemctl status rl-replicator` -> backlog queue depth 350k, worker flapping.
marta: restarted replicator worker on region-us-east: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/rl-replicator -n infra` now stable.
support-ops: customer messages sent to acme-corp and beta-inc. acme replied: "Thanks for the heads-up, our job is non-critical but please keep us posted."
leo: root cause summary (so far): quota-policy rollout reduced burst windows for some tenants -> scheduled job triggered retries causing 429s -> large retry and traffic surge exhausted model-proxy KV cache and caused OOMs and upstream resets -> gateway produced 502/503 -> overall 5xx spike.
kai (oncall): next steps: - revert the quota-policy change permanently after analysis - add canary gating for per-tenant defaults - add more robust token-bucket replica health alerts - write post-incident note with timeline and customer impact - propose automatic fallback routing when 429 > threshold
anjali: assigning follow-ups: marta -> postmortem draft (include logs + metrics), leo -> stability fixes for model-proxy (OOM tuning + circuit breaker), kai -> rollout gating + alerting, support-ops -> compile affected-customer list for CS handoff
marta: I'll open a postmortem ticket and add stakeholders. ETA for draft: EOD today.
kai (oncall): closing pager: monitoring for 30 more minutes then move to watch. leave thread for follow-ups.
incident-bot: Pager closed by kai (oncall) at 2024-11-02T14:30:49Z :resolved
support-ops: adding final customer comms template to thread: "We experienced a transient increase in error rates affecting inference requests between 14:05 and 14:25 UTC due to a misapplied quota policy. Mitigations have been applied; if you see lingering errors, please reply here or open a support ticket." :thumbsup:
leo: adding some diagnostic commands we used for runbook: ```bash
# check 429 per tenant
redis-cli HGETALL tenant:tokens | jq .
# quick pod restarts
kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-proxy -n inference
# temporarily open burst
POST /internal/admin/rl/burst -d '{"tenant":"acme-corp","burst":2000}'
```
anjali: I'll track the replicator backlog root cause in a separate ticket. queueing follow-up.
kai (oncall): thanks team. leaving thread for async followups. will ping when postmortem exists.
